key_insight: Narrow, winding collagen pores drive pressure demand, while slowly exchanging side pockets can make outlet measurements overstate internal medium replacement.
engineering_relevance: Bioreactor design should account for inlet–outlet geometry and pore-scale retention when sizing pumps and assessing medium renewal.
method: Simulated flow and medium replacement in pores traced from a collagen image.
Combined flow simulations with curved-channel theory to estimate resistance and plug permeability.
Compared small-opening and uniform-face feeding, plus outlet and interior replacement times.
evidence_signal: Small-opening feeding required about seven times the pressure of uniform-face feeding at the same flow rate; in the strongest retention case, interior 99% replacement took nearly three times as long as outlet replacement.
watch_item: The reported ratios are geometry-dependent simulation results and should not be assumed universal across collagen plugs.
paper_title: Pressure demand and solute replacement in a collagen-plugged bioreactor
